title: /dev: The Council
content:
Welcome to the first League Classic community poll. Our goal with these polls is to involve you, the community, in the direction that we take League Classic. Questions in these polls cover two broad types:

Voting can be done in “The Council” tab in the League client and is open for seven days, with the first running from August 26 through September 2. Eligible players may answer each question and change their answers until the poll closes. Each point of voting power gives one vote on each question. We’ll publish the results after voting closes in the Patch Notes.

This first poll covers questions across a few areas: game length, item revivals, and some map features. You can skip questions if you don’t have an opinion about the topic.

title: Kia Accelerates Its Connection with New Generations by Entering the Esports Ecosystem Through League of Legends in Latin America
summary: Kia Accelerates Its Connection with New Generations by Entering the Esports Ecosystem Through League of Legends in Latin America  WebWire
content:
Kia Central & South America has become an official sponsor of the LCS and CBLOL, two of the most important League of Legends leagues in the Americas

The partnership strengthens the brands connection with an industry that brings together more than 300 million players across Latin America

Kia launches Runes to Road, a regional activation designed to bring League of Legends fans closer to the action

Participants from Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru will have the opportunity to compete for an exclusive experience at the championship finals in October

The gaming industry has become one of the most significant cultural and entertainment phenomena in the world. Latin America is currently home to more than300 million playersand continues to establish itself as one of the fastest-growing regions in the sector, driven by a young, highly connected population with strong participation in digital communities.As esports continue evolving from a form of entertainment into a global cultural phenomenon, Kia recognizes a unique opportunity to connect with consumers seeking relevant, innovative experiences aligned with their interests.The gaming community shares many of the attributes that have defined Kias evolution as a brand:

Immersive experiences that inspire movement

title: "We can break even and be self-sustaining within Riot" – The firm behind League of Legends is "super close" to making esports sustainable
summary: "We can break even and be self-sustaining within Riot" – The firm behind League of Legends is "super close" to making esports sustainable &nbs...
content:
Riot Games' publishing and esports boss, John Needham, on the journey to profitability, Riot's transmedia ambitions, and why it allowed gambling sponsorship

Riot Games' esports business still isn't profitable.

This has been the case for a long time, and historically it hasn'tnecessarilybeen a problem for the League of Legends giant; at various points in the past, then-head of esports John Needham explained that his firmwanted to ensure the broader ecosystem, including the various esports teams, was profitable. But the aim was for esports to be a sustainable business in its own right.

That business is now "super close" to being profitable. What's changed? Needham –now head of publishing and esports at Riot– says the firm has adjusted how it operates its pro-gaming business since 2020.

"Coming out of the pandemic, we were in this esports winter," he tellsGamesIndustry.biz.

"The sponsorship business was weak, teams were having a hard time getting capital and investment in their business. We pivoted our business model away from sponsorships to digital items; that was a big positive move for teams. Teams also adjusted how much they were spending. The team business is in as good a place as it has ever been, now, and we are trying to do other things to allow teams to make alternate sources of revenue."
